snow_master.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized-concept. Revise the supplied RANK 5 miniature illustration to feel unmistakably like a rich little SNOW WORLD, rather than a sugar-crystal cavern.
EDIT TARGET: Image 1 is the current rank-5 art. Keep its portrait dimensions and framing, entire low circular white ceramic display plinth, plinth ellipse/position/diameter, empty white background and elevated front-left three-quarter viewpoint. Preserve the softly detailed lofi pixel-painted illustration language and muted ivory / blue-gray / turquoise / pale amber palette.

Main transformation: the sugar cube has COMPLETELY MATURED into a natural snowy alpine micro-landscape. Remove the squared-off rear-left sugar cap, the cube silhouette, and ALL conspicuous coarse sugar-granule crusts from the completed terrain. Do not merely sprinkle snow over the existing block. Resculpt the upper and outer mass into a rounded asymmetrical snow-covered ridge with two or three gentle irregular small peaks, deep layered snow blankets, wind-carved snowdrifts, soft overhanging cornices and powdery banks. Make the OUTDOOR SNOW TERRAIN a major visual presence: broad plush powder snow surfaces and curving ridgelines occupy the upper half of this world. Fine wind-sculpted snow texture rather than faceted sugar lumps. A few very small heavily snow-laden conifers on the upper-left slope and near the rear ridge reinforce the winter landscape; trees are sparse secondary details, not a forest covering the subject.
The lower front opens naturally into the existing inviting blue ice grotto: show a wide accessible snow-framed entrance with natural icy ledges, a few icicles, slim supporting ice columns, and a small still turquoise sheltered pool visible inside. Keep a couple of deeper connected recesses, but reduce the giant exposed lake/cathedral effect: snow-covered land should dominate, the water is a quiet feature inside the front grotto. Three detached thin ice plates on the inner pool, two gently touching. Keep three tiny winter songbirds as small supporting residents on snow-covered entrance ledges. Bird anatomy subtle and small, never mascot size. Their snow ledges have a few tiny footprints.
Powder snow collects on every upward-facing ledge. A few delicate snowflakes drift across the miniature itself, not a blizzard across the whole white background. Soft blue and lavender snow shadows give depth; muted peach dawn sunlight brushes a few snow ridges and filters into the grotto, with subtle reflected light on the ice. Quiet, intimate, restful, lofi winter atmosphere, sheltered rather than harsh or scary.
IMPORTANT: this is the final rank, so there is NO obligation to preserve any recognizable sugar cube shape or material. The whole natural landscape must feel like a satisfying physical transformation, not an unchanged cube decorated with objects. Do not introduce a town, buildings, houses, bridges, stairs, Christmas ornaments, lamps, furniture, people, extra animals or an ocean around the plinth. No lettering, UI, labels, border or watermark. Avoid glossy photorealistic 3D, cartoon outlines, childish picture-book style, oversaturated glowing blue crystals or dark cavern horror. The complete world remains neatly contained on the original dry white circular display base.

Use case: style-transfer / stylized-concept.
IMAGE ROLES: Image 1 is the CURRENT STAGE EDIT TARGET. Image 2 is the revised RANK-5 WINTER-WORLD MASTER; match its pixel scale, snowy material design and fixed circular-plinth presentation, but do not copy the fully grown scenery into this early stage. Image 3 is the user's PRIMARY DRAWING STYLE REFERENCE, the lofi rooftop pixel illustration: match its hand-painted pixel clusters, subdued matte materials, clear restrained shadows and fine texturing, NOT its city, nighttime or characters.
Redraw the stage as part of the same five-rank sequence, with the exact portrait 3:4 framing, fixed slightly elevated front-left camera, full white ceramic circular display plinth and pure white empty background. Keep the plinth ellipse, diameter and center consistent with the master. This is a real earlier physical growth form, no obscuring fog or reveal mask. Small cube progressively becomes a snowy natural mountain grotto.
Use clearly visible but detailed hand-placed square pixel clusters, crisp stepped contours, restrained dithering and limited local color ramps at the same scale as image 2. Not smooth airbrushed rendering or rounded 3D sculpture; no sugary pebble mosaic or polygon gemstone shading. Native-resolution pixel painting made at roughly 360x480 and cleanly enlarged. Snow and frost are formed by connected 2D pixel shapes; water, where present, uses horizontal pixel reflections. Preserve winter DAYLIGHT, not night: ivory/cool-white snow, muted blue/lavender shadows, shaded navy-blue ice interiors, soft peach edge light, subdued turquoise water. No town, houses, lamps, desk, humans, Christmas decorations, UI, status bars, black phone margins, lettering, numbers, labels, watermark or border. Entire world stays on the white circular platform. No ocean around it. No future-stage animals or objects.
RANK 1 — one ordinary slightly chipped rough SUGAR CUBE, small and centered, about one-third of the canvas width, sitting low on the mostly empty plinth. Keep the simple sugar-cube shape of image 1 and the little pile of loose sugar grains beneath its front chip. Render the sugar in the new matte pixel-art style with fine coarse-grain white pixels and blue-gray shadow patches, not smooth shiny 3D or huge crystal pebbles. No snow landscape yet; this is the starting seed. NO cave, through-hole, water, icicles, trees, birds or extra scenery. The chip is shallow granular sugar, not an opening into a cave.

Use case: style-transfer.
IMAGE 1 = EDIT TARGET: the current snowy miniature world at its final rank.
IMAGE 2 = PRIMARY STYLE REFERENCE: the attached lofi rooftop pixel illustration. Match its DRAWING LANGUAGE, not its subject.
Redraw image 1 as if it were made by the same pixel artist who drew image 2. This must be a substantial material/rendering change, not a light filter over a smooth 3D image.

PRESERVE: the portrait composition; white empty background; full low circular white display base; fixed elevated front-left three-quarter viewpoint; naturally irregular snow-covered mountain ridge with a few tiny snow-covered conifers; the wide front opening exposing a sheltered blue ice grotto, columns, icicles, layered ledges and a quiet turquoise pool; three thin detached ice floes and three TINY winter birds on snowy entrance ledges. Preserve the snow-focused revised design with NO sugar-cube silhouette, NO squared sugar cap, NO coarse sugar-grain crusts. Scenery is the focus. Do not add the city, neon signs, houses, person, desk, lamps, UI, text, status bar or black phone margins from image 2.

STYLE CHANGE: use fine but clearly VISIBLE PIXEL CLUSTERS across ALL objects, consistent crisp stepped contours, hand-placed square color patches, selectively dithered shadows, restrained small-scale texture. Think richly detailed lofi indie-game background pixel art made at roughly 360x480 and cleanly enlarged, rather than rounded digital sculpture. Match the rooftop reference's matte materials, simplified believable silhouettes, limited local color ramps, atmospheric depth and quiet lived-in feeling. Snow should be modeled with connected 2D pixel shapes and blue-violet shadow planes, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, photorealistic snow, polygonal gemstone facets, sugary mosaic pebbles or glossy 3D render surfaces. Water reflections should be short horizontal pixel strokes. The few tiny birds must share the same pixel scale as the whole scene, with understated pixel silhouettes; no larger smooth cartoon birds.

LIGHT AND COLOR: keep it a SNOWY DAYLIGHT WORLD on a WHITE BACKGROUND, not a nighttime scene. Translate the reference's gentle warm/cool contrast into ivory and cool white snow, subdued slate blue/lavender shadows, deep blue shaded grotto interiors, muted teal water and small pale amber sunlit ice edges. Soft peach daylight enters the roof opening. Richer midtones and clearer shadow shapes than the edit target, while retaining restful winter brightness. Do not flood the snow with orange light. Keep the miniature intimate, lofi, snowy, contemplative, not bright toy-like, childish, pastel storybook or hyperrealistic.

No lettering, labels, border, watermark or app UI. Output one finished portrait illustration, same framing and aspect as image 1.
